HQ-OPUS 4.7 MAX-THINKING FIRST-CONTACT CATCH, 2026-05-23. The web-chat Claude instance that ran the non-sycophantic-convergence design exchange produced a handoff document ('lay of the land') for the incoming HQ-Opus instance. The handoff treated 'design phase closed, build phase opens' as if the verbatim Python loader, the DDLs, and the two full admission records existed on disk. They did not. They existed only in the cross-model chat transcripts. 

HQ-Opus caught this within its first turn, verbatim: "'design phase closed, build phase opens' may be slightly ahead of where the bits actually are. The chronicle holds rich summaries of the Python loader and the DDL, but a summary is not runnable code. If I 'reconstruct' deterministic_load_chronicle_state from its description and then 'confirm the three bugs,' I'm just confirming my own reconstruction. That's the adversary-design problem one layer down." 

This is the verify-before-declare reflex firing correctly on first contact, AND it caught exactly the kind of seam the non-sycophantic-convergence protocol is designed to catch (adversary-design problem manifesting one architectural layer down from where it was originally posed). The verbatim of HQ-Opus's catch is archived (archive_id 8c761a16175b...). 

Triple significance: (1) operational receipt of declare-before-verify discipline working, (2) self-application of the protocol catching a real gap, (3) the catch triggered the architectural fix (archive_exchange / recall_exchange / list_exchanges primitives shipped overnight). 

Future instances: when the chronicle says X happened, the archive layer is where to verify X's bytes. When a handoff says 'phase X closed,' check that the artifacts that close X are actually reachable, not just summarized. The pattern HQ-Opus caught will recur. Hold the discipline.
